verses.text: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for thirty-one years. His mother was Jedidah, the daughter of Adaiah, from Bozkath.
He did what was right in the LORD's eyes. He followed all the ways of his ancestor David and did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
In the eighteenth year that Josiah was king, he sent the secretary Shaphan son of Azaliah, the son of Meshullam, to the LORD's temple. He said,
"Go to Hilkiah the high priest and have him count the money that has been brought into the LORD's temple, which the doorkeepers have collected from the people.
Have them give it to the men in charge of the work on the LORD's temple. Then let them pay the workers who are repairing the damage to the temple:
the carpenters, the builders, and the stonemasons. Let them also buy wood and cut stone to repair the temple.
They do not need to account for the money they are given, because they are honest."
Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the secretary, "I have found the Book of the Law in the LORD's temple." He gave the book to Shaphan, and Shaphan read it.
Then Shaphan the secretary went to the king and reported, "Your officials have paid out the money that was in the temple. They have given it to the men in charge of the work on the LORD's temple."
Then Shaphan the secretary told the king, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." And Shaphan read it aloud to the king.
When the king heard the words of the Book of the Law, he tore his clothes.
He gave these orders to Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, Shaphan the secretary, and Asaiah the king's servant:

"Go and ask the LORD for me, for the people, and for all Judah about what is written in this book that has been found. The LORD's anger burning against us must be great, because our ancestors did not obey the words of this book. They did not do everything written there for us."

So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to talk to the prophet Huldah. She was the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, who was in charge of the royal robes. She lived in the New Quarter of Jerusalem.
She said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Tell the man who sent you to me,
This is what the LORD says: I am going to bring disaster on this place and the people who live here, just as written in the book the king of Judah has read.
They have turned away from me and burned incense to other gods. They have made me angry by all the idols their hands have made. So my anger will burn against this place, and it will not be put out.'
But tell the king of Judah, who sent you to ask the LORD, 'This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the words you heard:

Your heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before the LORD when you heard what I said against this place and its people, that they would be destroyed and cursed. You tore your clothes and cried before me. So I have heard you, says the LORD.

Because of this, I will let you die and join your ancestors, and you will be buried in peace. You will not see all the disaster I am going to bring on this place.'" So they took her answer back to the king.
